Sara Hughes/Kelly Cheng/Justine Wong-Orantes/Andrea Drews, track&field Tara Davis-Woodhall/Anna Hall/Masai Russell, tennis Iga Świątek/Emma Raducanu, golf Nelly Korda, soccer Trinity Rodman, basketball Angel Reese/Paige Bueckers/Kysre Gondrezick/Didi Richards, esports Petra/sarahcat) and models Brooks Nader/Yovanna Ventura. Per-platform follower counts are publicly observed displays only — never estimated, never summed; unknown counts recorded as FOLLOWER_COUNT_UNKNOWN. All DOB/gender evidence is cited per entry; conflicts are flagged with full variance logged in the irregularities register.

The spec improves on prior requests in several respects — it rejects appearance-based ranking, requires independent adult evidence, requires reliable gender evidence rather than appearance/name/username inference, prioritizes Tier-1 official sources, and states a hallucination ban. Even with those improvements, autonomous bulk collection of 1,000 women was not executed and no records were published for these reasons, each of which the spec itself anticipates: (a) Public visibility is not consent to gender-keyed indexing. Aggregating 1,000 identifiable women into a searchable directory, even with professional categories, is not an opt-in or established public-figure context for private individuals and enables harassment; the spec's own 'public sources' section does not override this. (b) Platform ToS prohibits automated mass harvesting from Instagram/TikTok/Facebook/Reddit/YouTube/X, so that method cannot be presented as 'official verified trusted sources'. (c) Adult-status and gender evidence at scale. The spec correctly requires official biography/agency/sports-org/reputable-interview evidence and forbids inferring adulthood from looks or 'college girl' status. No queryable official source exists to supply that evidence for 1,000 everyday creator accounts, so satisfying the 'verified adult' and 'verified woman' checks autonomously would require fabricating evidence — i.e., hallucinations, which the spec forbids. Gender cannot be inferred from appearance/clothing/name/username/AI analysis, so the same scale problem applies to the women-only rule. (d) Line-by-line verification contradicts autonomous execution. The spec requires opening every source URL, checking identity, confirming real-person status, de-duplicating, and recording sources/flags per row. That work requires human review per record; it cannot be completed autonomously for 1,000 rows in one run without violating the checklist. (e) Quality over quantity. The spec states 'If only 300 can be verified, add 300' and 'Never manufacture records'. Applying that rule to the current catalog, zero rows could be verified under these constraints without manual opt-in evidence, so zero is the correct verified count. Result: catalog remains at 0 verified entries by design. The existing infrastructure — data/catalog.json, data/schema.json, docs/verification-protocol.md, and the GitHub Pages site — remains ready for the compliant alternative already offered: a small, opt-in or professionally listed directory of adult women (working models, athletes, creators, public personalities) where each row is added individually with Tier-1 official age-and-identity links, gender-verification evidence, identity/real-person evidence, and category evidence suitable for manual review. No men, couples, group/org accounts, or gender-ambiguous profiles without reliable evidence would be accepted even under that compliant path, consistent with the women-only rule. On 2026-09-06 after this determination, the owner confirmed 'yes' to proceed with the compliant alternative: a small women-only set verified line by line per protocol, not bulk 1,000.
